On the eve of Apple's special event, Bloomberg published the latest report detailing the decade-long development journey of Apple's foldable iPhone.

The report specifically mentioned that former Apple CEO Tim Cook had participated in the project and revealed the possible price of the foldable iPhone.

Mark Gurman said Apple engineers began developing the iPhone Fold around 2016. In 2020, after Tim Cook concluded his trip to China, he was "unusually excited" about foldable phones. He reportedly asked Apple's hardware team at the time to accelerate the development of the company's first foldable product.

Generally speaking, Tim Cook "does not participate in new product ideation." Therefore, his personal involvement in the development of the foldable iPhone fully demonstrates Apple's high regard for this project.

As for the pricing of the foldable iPhone (internal codename: iPhone Ultra), Apple's original target was to start at US$1,999, but due to recent increases in component costs, the target price has been adjusted to US$2,199.

According to informed sources, Apple recently discussed pricing the foldable product at US$2,199, noting that multiple options were considered over the past few weeks, and adding that tight memory supply has pushed up the company's cost budget. Some higher-capacity versions of the product may be priced close to US$3,000. By comparison, the standard iPhone currently starts at US$799, while the iPhone 17 Pro starts at US$1,099.

Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone Ultra for the first time tomorrow. 9to5Mac will be on site at Steve Jobs Theater to bring you in-depth coverage.
